slides.heading: Year 1 — Autumn 2, Week 1
slides.sub: New content taught directly, practised in words/sentences and applied in reading and dictation.

slides.heading: Mon
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "ew" (/uː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="stew" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="stew"><ellipse cx="-82.8" cy="-55" rx="14" ry="20" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><ellipse cx="82.8" cy="-55" rx="14" ry="20" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M-90 -33Q-90 0 0 0Q90 0 90 -33z" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><ellipse cx="0" cy="-33" rx="90" ry="16" fill="#c99a63" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="3.5"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Grew the Seed pushes up out of the soil a little further every day, stretching out a long 'ew' as he grows.

character.name: Grew the Seed
character.blurb: Grew the Seed is a small leaf-green seed who stretches taller each morning, humming 'ew' as he unfurls.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'oo' in moon — 'ew' usually appears at the end of a word.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'e', then 'w', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children start crouched low then slowly stretch upward with arms reaching, saying a long 'ew' as they rise.
slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="stew" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="stew"><ellipse cx="-82.8" cy="-55" rx="14" ry="20" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><ellipse cx="82.8" cy="-55" rx="14" ry="20" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><path d="M-90 -33Q-90 0 0 0Q90 0 90 -33z" fill="#c3ced6" stroke="#3b4954" stroke-width="3.5"/><ellipse cx="0" cy="-33" rx="90" ry="16" fill="#c99a63" stroke="#6d4318" stroke-width="3.5"/></svg>

slides.tip: The 'ou' is the tricky part: it doesn't say any of its usual sounds here. Sound out the rest and remember that part.

slides.heading: Tue
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "oe" (/əʊ/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="-90 -110 180 180" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="toe" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" class="wp-icon" data-picture="toe"><ellipse cx="0" cy="0" rx="8" ry="5" fill="#155a7c" opacity="0.42" stroke="none"/><circle cx="-6" cy="-7" r="2.6" fill="#155a7c" opacity="0.42" stroke="none"/><circle cx="0" cy="-9" r="2.6" fill="#155a7c" opacity="0.42" stroke="none"/><circle cx="6" cy="-7" r="2.6" fill="#155a7c" opacity="0.42" stroke="none"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Rowan Duckling waddles along on her webbed toes, saying a rounded 'oe' with every step.

character.name: Rowan Duckling
character.blurb: Rowan Duckling has bright sunflower-yellow feathers and waddles along on webbed feet, calling 'oe' as she paddles.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'oa' in boat — 'oe' is a less common ending used in only a handful of words.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'o', then 'e', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children waddle in place with feet turned slightly out, saying 'oe' with each waddling step.

slides.heading: Wed
slides.objective: Learn the new sound "au" (/ɔː/) and start reading and spelling words that use it.

slides.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 100 100" width="320" height="320" role="img" aria-label="astronaut" class="wp-icon wp-raster" data-picture="astronaut_s"><image href="data:image/png;base64," x="0" y="0" width="100" height="100" preserveAspectRatio="xMidYMid meet"/></svg>

slides.mnemonic: Augustus Acorn drops from the branch every autumn with a soft thud and a low 'au' as he lands.

character.name: Augustus Acorn
character.blurb: Augustus Acorn wears one sandy stripe across his cap, and he only falls in autumn, landing with a gentle 'au'.

slides.pronunciation_note: This is another way to write the same sound children already know as 'or' in for and 'aw' in saw — 'au' usually appears in the middle of a word.
slides.formation_cue: Write 'a', then 'u', close together — two letters, one sound.
slides.action: Children raise one hand high like a branch and let it drop slowly to their side, saying 'au' as it lands.

slides.heading: Thu
slides.objective: Extra practice blending and segmenting everything taught this week — no new content today.

slides.heading: Fri
slides.objective: Revisit everything taught this week, read the matched decodable book, and check how securely it has been learned.
